doc.title: Jimmy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Versatility for young players: Tia Fuller with Beyonce
summary: Heath agrees young musicians must be flexible and cites his student Tia Fuller.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Do you think that young people today need to be, I don’t know, willing to embrace other kinds of music and, I don’t know if you want to use the dreaded word, crossover…
… in order to get in front of audiences do you have to be flexible—more flexible—today.

They do. I have a student now, she’s a great saxophonist, and she’s playing with Beyonce. She’s been with Beyonce, Tia Fuller, her name is. [She’s a] great saxophonist. I met her when I went to Spellman College, and then she left Spellman and went to somewhere in Colorado to another college. She can play jazz, but she’s playing what is necessary with Beyonce in order to make a living, and she’s doing quite well.
